text:
alex: Telemetry -> spike in DNS resolution failures from several GPU edge nodes in ap-northeast-1 around 00:20 UTC. Alert group `resolv_errors` tripped for model-fetch and imagepull names.
Maya: Acknowledged. Any obvious pattern (AZ, node image, recent deploys)? :thinking:
alex: Narrowed to ap-northeast-1a and 1c. Same k8s pool, mixed GPU SKUs. Only some pods show NX/timeout.
Sam: Did we change egress/SNAT port behaviour last night? I pushed the ephemeral port reuse tweak to reduce port exhaustion for GPU pools.
jin: Yep, that rollout happened ~00:15 UTC. It trims ephemeral range and enables port reuse on the NAT hosts.
Maya: Could port reuse disturb UDP DNS responses? If replies land on a different tuple because of reuse, the stub resolver might see a timeout or garbage.
Sam: That's the suspicion. High multiplexing + small ephemeral space -> conntrack collisions. UDP DNS can be dropped or return to wrong socket.
alex: I repro locally on a test node. Command and output:
```$ dig internal-registry.svc.cluster.local @10.0.0.10
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> internal-registry.svc.cluster.local @10.0.0.10
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; flags: qr aa rd; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 0
;; SERVER: 10.0.0.10#53(10.0.0.10)
;; WHEN: Wed Mar 18 00:27:00 UTC
;; MSG SIZE  rcvd: 56
```
No ANSWER records despite server responding.
jin: Checked /etc/resolv.conf on affected vs healthy nodes: some nodes use systemd-resolved stub (127.0.0.53); others use kube-dns IP directly. Mixed resolver stacks across same pool.
Sam: Mixed stacks + SNAT port reuse = nasty nondeterministic failures. systemd-resolved uses a local UDP socket; if conntrack maps incorrectly the process never sees the reply.
alex: Kernel logs show conntrack TIME_WAIT churn and lots of UDP mismatched packets around the timeframe.
router-bot: [route-change] egress-nat-range updated by @Sam — ephemeral ports reduced to 1024-61000 at 2026-03-18T00:15:12Z
Maya: Proposal: temporarily revert the ephemeral range in ap-northeast-1 AZs to previous larger range and observe. Can we do a scoped revert per AZ?
Sam: Starting scoped revert for 1a now (only that AZ). Will monitor DNS NX rate.
jin: Parallel action: I'll inventory node images and make resolver behaviour consistent (disable systemd stub on image X or ensure kube-dns IP pinned). We should avoid mixing resolver stacks in same node pool.
alex: For debugging I'm capturing pcap + conntrack before/after revert:
```sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 udp port 53 -w /tmp/dns-udp.pcap
sudo conntrack -L | grep udp | grep 53 > /tmp/conntrack-dns.txt
```
Sam: Revert applied to 1a. Monitoring metrics.
alex: Telemetry shows NX/timeouts drop in 1a within ~3m. 1c still elevated. Sam, can you roll revert to 1c next?
Sam: Rolling 1c now.
jin: Long-term mitigations we should track: enforce consistent resolver stack across images, enable DNS over TCP fallback in kube-dns, evaluate DoT/DoH for inter-node lookups where possible, and add conntrack tuning for high multiplexing pools.
Maya: Also add an alert: DNS NX/timeout rate per AZ and per node-pool so we catch this pattern earlier. Put threshold low for GPU dense pools.
alex: Collected pcaps + conntrack dumps and uploaded to S3 (link in ticket). Errors down to baseline after full revert.
deploy-bot: rollback egress-nat-range for ap-northeast-1a applied by @Sam
Sam: Full revert done for 1a & 1c. Observability shows resolution rate normalized.
jin: I'll open INFRA ticket to standardize resolver image behaviour and add a preflight check in the GPU pool rollout job to ensure resolver homogeneity.
Maya: I'll own the kube-dns config change to enable TCP fallback and a short RFC for DoT evaluation.
alex: Action items recap (short):
- Sam: revert/verify egress port-range per AZ (done)
- Jin: audit node images + enforce resolver stack consistently (in progress)
- Alex: share pcaps/conntrack and paste incident summary in INFRA-832 (done)
- Maya: kube-dns TCP fallback + alert + DoT RFC (owned)
Closing notes: recommend we avoid rolling aggressive SNAT port compression while node pools have mixed resolver stacks. Will follow up in INFRA-832. :thumbsup:
